chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah al-Dahqan, from Durust, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), who said:
The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) ate the melon with sugar, and ate the melon with fresh dates.

key_terms.الرُّطَبِ: Fresh dates (dates at the rutab stage)

ai.seo_question: Did the Prophet Muhammad eat melon with sugar or dates?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the prominent chain of al-Kulayni, highlights the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) consumption of melon with sugar and fresh dates, illustrating the permissibility of combining sweet fruits in Islamic dietary law. In Shia scholarly tradition, this serves as a practical precedent for culinary preferences and the moderation of sweetness, reinforcing the concept of *tayyibat* (pure and good foods) mentioned in the Quran. It also subtly underscores the cultural context of Medina, where dates were a staple, and their combination with other fruits was both nutritious and culturally accepted.
